# Identity contract + CLI

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Agent / harness · **Label:** `feature:identity-contract` · **Epic:** [#26](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/26) · **Tickets:** 7 (6S 1M)

Defines how any agent platform sends a user's identity to Warden, and ships a small `warden identity` CLI so any agent, script or harness can get a token and route through the worker. Warden stays platform-neutral: a harness only needs an OIDC ID token from the configured issuer and a proxy URL. Phase 1 is attribution only, so a missing or bad token never blocks a request and default-deny policy is unchanged. `warden identity exec` runs a command behind a loopback forwarder that keeps the short-lived token out of the command's environment and argv and refreshes it before expiry.

## How we build it

- Contract v1 (docs/identity-contract.md): an OIDC ID token from the worker's `identity.issuer` whose `aud` contains `identity.audience`, signed RS256 or ES256, with `sub` required and `email`, `groups` and `sid` expected. The doc separates what the worker enforces (iss, aud, exp/nbf with 60s skew, alg) from what is issuer configuration (1h ID-token lifetime, groups claim). Identity is keyed on (iss, sub); email is a display attribute. Later phases may add to v1 but never change a v1 header or claim.
- Getting the token from Dex: cross-client trust, with scopes `openid email profile groups offline_access audience:server:client_id:<worker audience>` on the confidential `agent-harness` client (harness platforms) or the public device-code `warden-cli` client (user machines). `groups` and `offline_access` are required, or the token has no groups claim and cannot be refreshed. The reference Dex config (W-P1-DEX-01) keeps the data-plane audience `warden` separate from the console client `warden-console`: `warden` never logs anyone in, a console login token never carries aud `warden`, and the CP console accepts only aud `warden-console`, so a harness token is never a console token. Workers should set `identity.allowedAZP: [agent-harness, warden-cli]`.
- Transport: `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` on CONNECT (Bearer also accepted), which clients send from a proxy URL `http://session:<token>@<worker>:8080`. The fallback `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer <token>` only works on connections where the worker terminates TLS; on raw tunnels it cannot be read, so harnesses must prefer Proxy-Authorization (both headers are stripped before forwarding, already on main). Attribution is bound per tunnel at CONNECT time. Only https through CONNECT is supported: the worker drops any other request line as unsupported_protocol (internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn). Transparent mode (#376, `proxy.mode`) has no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization, so there only X-Warden-Identity on terminated traffic attributes, and `warden identity env` (proxy variables) does not apply to a transparently intercepted agent. Limits already enforced on main: token at most 16 KiB (reason too_large), CONNECT request line at most 8 KiB (414), whole header block at most 64 KiB with a 10 s deadline (431, deny reason malformed_connect, detail headers_too_large).
- Harness duties: keep the IdP login and refresh token out of the agent's reach (another uid or a sidecar), give each user's processes only that user's token, refresh before expiry, recycle connections after a refresh, and never put the token in prompts, model context, logs, argv or tool output. Phase 1 limit, stated plainly: a token placed in HTTPS_PROXY is readable by the agent's own tools and is a snapshot that goes stale after about 1h. That is tolerated for `warden identity env` while P1 is attribute-only. `warden identity exec` (W-P1-IDC-06, on the forwarder from W-P1-IDC-04) removes both limits in P1: it runs the child behind a loopback forwarder that holds the user's ID token in memory, takes a fresh token from the refreshing client for every new CONNECT and injects it, so the token is never in the parent's or the child's environment or argv. A tunnel opened before a refresh keeps its original token (attribution is bound per tunnel), so clients recycle connections. P2 extends the same forwarder with agent tokens (W-P2-RCP-02/06).
- `warden identity` CLI: new package internal/identityclient (library: config, discovery, device login, locked file cache, Token/Status; W-P1-IDC-02) plus a new cobra subtree in cmd/proxy that ignores the worker `--config` (commands and env renderer; W-P1-IDC-05). Config comes from flags, `WARDEN_IDENTITY_*` env vars, or `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/identity.yaml`. Subcommands: `login` (OIDC discovery and RFC 8628 device-code grant via golang.org/x/oauth2, public client by default, optional secret only from `--client-secret-env NAME`), `token` (prints a valid ID token, refreshing at 2/3 of exp-iat, never prompts), `status` (prints iss, sub, email, groups and exp, never the token), `env --worker host:port` (HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy with session credentials, NO_PROXY for loopback, optional CA variables, token from cache, `--token-stdin` or `--token-file`), `logout`, and `exec` (W-P1-IDC-06).
- Cache safety: refresh and ID tokens live in a 0600 file inside a 0700 directory, written by temp file, fsync and rename. The CLI refuses a cache file readable by group or others. Refresh runs under an exclusive lock and re-reads the cache after taking it, because Dex rotates refresh tokens on use. If the issuer is unreachable, `token` serves the cached token while it is valid and warns on stderr. Exit code 2 means login is required; 3 means the issuer is unreachable and no valid cached token remains. Plain-http issuers are accepted only on a loopback host (the dev issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex`); any other http issuer is refused and there is no override flag. Tokens, device codes and IdP error bodies are never printed to stderr or logged; `--verbose` shows only an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint.
- Back-compat and upgrades: everything is opt-in. With no `identity` block, workers behave exactly as today, and existing recipes and proxy URLs without credentials keep working. The new `identity` commands change no flag or behaviour of `run` or `control-plane`. P2 extends internal/identityclient with agent keys, RFC 8693 exchange and `identity forward`, and adds `--agent-id` and `--run-as` to the P1 `identity exec`; the contract doc records that v1 Dex tokens must stay accepted on upgrade for workers that already set `identity.issuer` (see open question on W-P2-WBND-01).

## Done when

On the shared L2 identity stack (`make e2e-identity-up`: control plane, Dex with LDAP, an attribute-mode worker, a curl agent on an internal-only network with no direct route out and no Dex access), the test `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentitySmoke` routes the curl agent through the worker using `warden identity env --token-stdin` with a seeded user's token. The CP traffic API filtered by that user returns events carrying their sub, email and groups with identity_status=valid. Requests with no token and with a bad token are still allowed and recorded as `none` and `invalid`. No token appears in test output, CLI output or worker logs. `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentityExec` shows `warden identity exec --worker <worker> -- curl https://<allowed host>` attributed to the same user, while the child's environment and argv contain no token (unit tests prove the token is refreshed without restarting the child). docs/identity-contract.md matches the code constants (`go test ./internal/proxy -run TestContractDocMatchesConstants`) and the `warden identity` commands it shows parse against the CLI.

### 1/7 · W-P1-IDC-01

**Write the agent identity contract for harness builders**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#27](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/27)

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26) defines how any agent platform sends a user's identity to Warden. This ticket (#27) writes the contract for harness builders: exactly what token to send, how to send it, what the worker does with it, and what the harness must never do. It documents behaviour from p1-verify-token and from the `warden identity` CLI, so it merges last in this feature. Its constants come from W-P1-VRFY-01 (statuses, reasons), W-P1-VRFY-02 (header names), W-P1-VRFY-08 (modes); the commands come from W-P1-IDC-06 (exec, which brings IDC-05 login/token/status/env and IDC-04); the documented flow is proven by the L2 smoke W-P1-IDC-03. Siblings: IDC-02 (library), IDC-05 (CLI), IDC-04 (forwarder), IDC-06 (exec), IDC-03 and IDC-07 (L2 tests). Out of scope: any code change other than two doc-drift tests.

What to build: docs/identity-contract.md plus links, and tests that keep the doc in line with the code.

**Requirements**

- Version marker `Contract v1`, with a rule that later phases may add to v1 but never change a v1 header or claim. A short 'Upgrading to Phase 2' section says that v1 Dex tokens must stay accepted for workers that already set `identity.issuer`.
- Token section: iss byte-identical to `identity.issuer`, aud contains `identity.audience`, RS256/ES256 only, exp/nbf with 60s skew, `sub` required, `email`/`groups`/`sid` expected. A table marks each rule as either enforced by the worker or issuer configuration (1h lifetime, groups claim). Lists the Dex scopes, including `groups` and `offline_access`. Identity is keyed on (iss, sub); email is display-only. Explains that the worker audience (`warden` in the reference config) is a data-plane-only client separate from the console client `warden-console`, and recommends `identity.allowedAZP` listing the harness and CLI clients.
- Transport section, with exact strings: `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` (username `session`, case-sensitive; Bearer also accepted) from the proxy URL `http://session:<token>@<worker>:8080`; fallback `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer <token>` only on TLS-terminated connections; both stripped before forwarding in every mode, including off (already enforced on main, #396); two valid identities with different sub give identity_status `conflict` and the request still proceeds in P1 (a 403 is reserved for P2 require mode); attribution bound per tunnel at CONNECT time; only https through CONNECT, plain HTTP_PROXY requests are denied (unsupported_protocol). Transparent mode (#376, `proxy.mode`) has no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization: there only `X-Warden-Identity` on terminated traffic carries identity, raw transparent tunnels stay anonymous, and `warden identity env` does not apply. Limits (already enforced on main): a token over 16 KiB is recorded as invalid with reason too_large; the CONNECT request line is capped at 8 KiB (414) and the whole header block at 64 KiB with a 10 s deadline, overflow gets 431 with deny reason `malformed_connect` (detail `headers_too_large`). A 16 KiB token base64-encoded in Basic credentials fits.
- Modes and statuses: per-agent `off|attribute` (`require` is rejected until Phase 2), identity_status `off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict` (W-P1-VRFY-01) and what the dashboard shows for each, the event fields user_sub, user_email, user_groups, user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status, identity_reason, the metric `warden_identity_verify_total{result,reason}` (Prometheus name of `warden.identity.verify.total`), and the query `/dashboard/api/traffic?user=`. Recommends alerting on the share of non-valid results per agent.
- Harness duties and a do-not list: IdP login and refresh token kept out of the agent's reach, one token per user, refresh before expiry, no tokens in prompts, model context, logs, argv, tool output or `curl -v` output. A 'Phase 1 limitation' callout covers the token in HTTPS_PROXY (readable by agent tools, stale after about 1h, plaintext agent-to-worker hop) and points to `warden identity exec` (W-P1-IDC-06), which keeps the token out of the child's env and argv and takes a fresh token for each new CONNECT; a tunnel opened before a refresh keeps its original token, so long-lived clients recycle connections.
- Client compatibility table: preemptive Basic from proxy-URL credentials (curl, Go net/http, Python requests, Node with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1) works; clients that send credentials only after a 407 challenge get no identity in P1 because the worker never challenges. Examples use the CA variables printed by `warden identity env --ca` and show tokens only as `eyJ...redacted`.
- Linked from README.md, docs/recipes/README.md and docs/identity-dex.md, and the contract doc links back to docs/identity-dex.md. Two machine checks keep it honest: a drift test for constants (below) and a command test that every `warden identity ...` command line shown in a fenced block parses against the real cobra tree.
- `warden identity exec` section (also summarised in docs/recipes/README.md 'Per-user identity'): the child runs behind a loopback forwarder that holds the token in memory and injects a fresh token on every new CONNECT, so the token is not in the child's environment or argv; a tunnel opened before a refresh keeps its original token; a child running as the same uid can still read the identity cache file, so use a separate uid (P2 adds `--run-as`).

**Implementation plan**

1. Write new docs/identity-contract.md with sections: Contract v1, Token, Getting a token (Dex), Transport, Lifetimes and limits, Modes and statuses, Observability, Harness duties, Phase 1 limitations, Client compatibility, Upgrading to Phase 2.
2. Copy header names, status values and mode names from the exported constants in internal/identity, internal/config and internal/proxy (added by W-P1-VRFY-01, VRFY-08 and VRFY-02) rather than retyping them.
3. Show runnable examples for `warden identity login`, `status`, `token`, `exec --worker 127.0.0.1:8080 -- curl ...` and `eval "$(warden identity env --worker 127.0.0.1:8080 --ca certs/proxy-ca.crt)"`, then curl, Python requests and Node.
4. Add links from README.md, docs/recipes/README.md (new 'Per-user identity' section) and docs/identity-dex.md.
5. Add the new internal/proxy/contract_doc_test.go (TestContractDocMatchesConstants): it reads ../../docs/identity-contract.md and fails if any exported header, mode, status or reason constant from internal/identity, internal/config and internal/proxy is missing from it, or the doc mentions a status that no constant defines. (It lives in internal/proxy so it may import identity, config and proxy without a layering violation.)
6. Add the new cmd/proxy/identity_doc_test.go (TestContractDocCommands): extract every fenced line starting with `warden identity` and check the subcommand and every flag exist in the cobra tree built by newRootCmd.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestContractDocMatchesConstants` passes, and fails (red first) when a constant such as the `conflict` status or `X-Warden-Identity` is renamed without updating the doc.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestContractDocCommands` passes, and fails when the doc shows a flag the CLI does not have.
- [ ] The documented flow works end to end: `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME='TestIdentitySmoke|TestIdentityExec'` passes (these tests are owned by W-P1-IDC-03 and W-P1-IDC-07; this ticket only merges after them).
- [ ] `grep -l 'identity-contract.md' README.md docs/recipes/README.md docs/identity-dex.md` lists all three files.
- [ ] `grep -E 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}' docs/identity-contract.md` returns nothing.
- [ ] The doc lists exactly the statuses off, none, valid, invalid, expired, unverified and conflict and the modes off and attribute, matching config validation in internal/config (covered by the drift test).
- [ ] The doc states the real limits and the transparent-mode gap: `grep -E '8 KiB|64 KiB|malformed_connect|transparent' docs/identity-contract.md` matches all four, and `grep -E '32 KiB|100 lines' docs/identity-contract.md` prints nothing.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 2/7 · W-P1-IDC-02

**Add internal/identityclient: config, discovery, device login, locked file cache, Token and Status**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#28](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/28)

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26) ships a `warden identity` CLI so any agent, script or harness can get a user token and route through the worker. This is the foundation ticket (#28): the library package internal/identityclient with everything the commands and the forwarder need, and no cobra code. It was split from the original M ticket #28: the cobra subtree, the env renderer and the exit codes moved to W-P1-IDC-05. It works with any standards OIDC issuer and never hard-codes Dex. It has no dependencies (the default `warden-cli` client id is documented, not imported from the Dex ticket). Siblings: IDC-05 (commands and env output), IDC-04 (loopback forwarder), IDC-06 (`identity exec`), IDC-03/07 (L2 tests), IDC-01 (docs). W-P2-RCP-01 later extends this package with agent keys and token exchange. Out of scope: cmd/proxy, env rendering, the forwarder.

What to build: the Config loader, OIDC discovery, the RFC 8628 device-code login, the 0600 file cache with an exclusive lock, and Client.Token/Status with typed errors. Architecture gate: every new package needs exactly one class in architecture.yaml (rule L8) and a zone (Z1); every new third-party module needs an entry in the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml; new HTTP routes are registered in a routes.go (rule X9). Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- New package internal/identityclient with exactly one architecture class and zone in architecture.yaml (it does file and network I/O; not `domain`), and golang.org/x/oauth2 in go.mod pinned to a release at least 2 weeks old, passing govulncheck, with an S3 `modules:` manifest entry (skip the entry if a sibling ticket such as W-P1-SSO-03 already added it; the allowed layers must cover both users). A cached `Token` call does no network I/O. The package has a _test.go (rule C3).
- `Config{Issuer, ClientID, Audience, ClientSecretEnv string; Scopes []string; CacheDir string}` and `LoadConfig(flags Flags, getenv func(string) string, readFile func(string) ([]byte, error)) (Config, error)`; precedence flags, then WARDEN_IDENTITY_ISSUER / _CLIENT_ID / _AUDIENCE / _SCOPES / _CACHE_DIR, then optional `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/identity.yaml`. Defaults: client id `warden-cli` (the public device-code client of the reference Dex config), audience `warden` (used only for the aud warning below; the Dex cross-client scope `audience:server:client_id:warden` is passed through Scopes as documented, never hard-coded), scopes `openid email profile groups offline_access` plus any added scopes. The client secret is read only from the environment variable NAMED by ClientSecretEnv, never a literal. The worker `--config` is never loaded.
- A plain-http issuer is accepted only when its host is loopback (`localhost`, 127.0.0.0/8, `::1`): the dev issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` works with no flag. Any other http issuer is refused with a clear error and there is no override flag or setting (the CLI runs on the host, so it never needs the CP/worker internal issuer URL). https issuers are always accepted. LoadConfig rejects an issuer with a query, fragment or userinfo.
- `Discover(ctx, *http.Client, issuer)` reads plain JSON discovery (no go-oidc), requires the discovered issuer to match byte for byte and https (or a loopback host), and returns the token and device_authorization endpoints.
- `Client{Config, HTTP *http.Client, Now func() time.Time, Log *slog.Logger}` with `Login(ctx, prompt io.Writer) error` running the device-code grant via golang.org/x/oauth2 (DeviceAuth, DeviceAccessToken), honouring `interval`, `slow_down` and `expires_in`, printing the verification URI and user code to the prompt writer only. Before caching, the ID token claims are parsed UNVERIFIED (the worker verifies) and `Login` returns warnings naming only the claim when `groups` is missing or aud lacks the configured audience.
- Cache: `<cache-dir>/<sha256(issuer|client_id)[:16]>.json` holds the refresh token, ID token and the local receipt time. `FileStore{Dir}` with `Load`, `Save` (temp file, fsync, rename; 0600 file in a 0700 directory) and `WithLock(fn)` using an exclusive flock on `<cache>.lock` (unix build tag; a stub for other platforms returns a clear error). A cache file readable by group or others is refused with an error naming the path. `Entry` (the JSON shape) is exported so tests can seed a cache.
- `Token(ctx) (TokenResult, error)` (TokenResult{IDToken string; Expiry time.Time; Warning string}) returns the cached ID token while less than 2/3 of exp-iat has passed (measured from local receipt time) and refreshes otherwise, holding the lock and RE-READING the cache after taking it (Dex rotates refresh tokens on use), persisting any rotated refresh token. It never prompts. Two concurrent callers cause exactly one refresh. If the issuer is unreachable and the cached token is still valid it returns it with a warning in `TokenResult.Warning`; typed errors `ErrLoginRequired` (no, expired or revoked refresh token) and `ErrIssuerUnreachable` (no valid cached token) let the caller choose exit codes 2 and 3.
- `Status() (StatusInfo, error)` returns iss, sub, email, groups, exp and the cache path, never the token. `Logout()` deletes the cache entry (and lock file).
- Secrets hygiene: tokens, device codes and IdP error bodies are never returned in error strings or logged (`oauth2.RetrieveError` is wrapped with the body dropped); the logger gets issuer, client id, scopes, expiry and an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint (`Fingerprint(token) string`) only.
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. go.mod: add golang.org/x/oauth2 (DeviceAuth, DeviceAccessToken and the refresh grant); add the architecture.yaml class, zone and manifest entry; run `go run ./cmd/archgen`.
2. New internal/identityclient/config.go and discovery.go: Config, Flags, LoadConfig, Discover.
3. New internal/identityclient/store.go (+ lock_unix.go and lock_other.go): FileStore, Entry, Load, Save, WithLock.
4. New internal/identityclient/client.go: Client, Login, Token, Status, Logout, typed errors, Fingerprint.
5. Tests in internal/identityclient/*_test.go against an httptest fake issuer (discovery, device_authorization with authorization_pending then slow_down then success, a refresh grant that rotates the refresh token) and a fake clock.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run 'TestDeviceLogin|TestDevicePollSlowDown|TestRefreshAtTwoThirds|TestTokenNoPrompt|TestIssuerDownServesCache'` passes: login stores a refresh token, slow_down raises the poll interval, `Token` refreshes exactly once after 2/3 of lifetime, an expired refresh token returns ErrLoginRequired without prompting, an unreachable issuer still returns a valid cached token with a warning and ErrIssuerUnreachable when none is valid.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/identityclient -run TestConcurrentRefreshSingleFlight` shows two concurrent Token() calls cause exactly one refresh request against a rotating fake issuer, and both get the same token.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestCacheFilePerms` checks the cache file is 0600 in a 0700 directory, and a cache chmodded to 0644 is refused with an error naming the path.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run 'TestHTTPIssuerLoopbackOnly|TestDiscoveryIssuerMismatch'` accepts `http://localhost:5556/dex` and `http://127.0.0.1:5556/dex`, rejects an http non-loopback issuer (no override exists), and rejects a discovery document whose issuer differs by one byte.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestNoSecretsInErrorsOrLogs` shows no substring of the ID token, refresh token, device code or IdP error body in any returned error or captured log line, with the logger at debug level.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestLoadConfigPrecedence` covers flags over env over file, the defaults, and that a literal client secret is impossible.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` passes with the new package class and the oauth2 manifest entry, and `scripts/check.sh` passes, including govulncheck.

### 3/7 · W-P1-IDC-03

**Add the L2 identity attribution smoke with a curl agent**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#29](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/29)

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26). This ticket (#29) proves, against real Dex and real containers, that a plain curl container with no agent framework can be attributed to a user through the `warden identity` CLI and the contract. It plays the harness: it gets a seeded LDAP user's token from Dex and hands it to `warden identity env --token-stdin` inside the agent. It was rewritten from a shell script, a bespoke compose file and a `scripts/check.sh --smoke-identity` flag into a Go test on the shared L2 identity stack from W-P1-DEX-04 (the stack, helpers and CI wiring now live there), and the worker/CP identity configuration is added here. Behaviour with a fake issuer is covered in process by the L1 scenarios (W-P1-VRFY-05); this test exists only because it needs real Dex, LDAP and an internal-only agent network. Depends on DEX-04 (stack), IDC-05 (the `identity env` command), VRFY-07 (worker verifies), VRFY-09 (events carry the user) and VRFY-04 (`?user=` on the CP traffic API). Out of scope: `identity exec` (IDC-07), console SSO (SSO-07), the stack itself.

What to build: the `identity:` block in the worker e2e config and the test file `test/e2e/identity/identity_smoke_test.go`. SafeDialer's private-IP block is not loosened.

- Edit `configs/config.e2e-identity-worker.yaml` (created by W-P1-DEX-04): add `identity:` with defaultMode `attribute`, issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex`, `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` (the worker container cannot reach `localhost:5556`; the issuer string stays the public one), audience `warden`, allowedAZP [agent-harness, warden-cli]; keep the allowlist to the fake upstream's host. No SSRF or private-IP setting is changed. The CP config needs no console block here.
- New `test/e2e/identity/identity_smoke_test.go` (build tag e2e) with tests named `TestIdentitySmoke*`, using the helpers from W-P1-DEX-04 (each test starts with `requireStack(t)`: blocked fails under CI and skips loudly locally): `dexToken(t, "alice")` for the token, fetched from the host at `http://localhost:5556` with no dialer override; the token is piped to the agent on stdin through `agentExec` running `sh -c 'eval "$(/opt/warden/warden identity env --worker worker-1:8080 --token-stdin --ca /etc/warden/certs/proxy-ca.crt)" && curl -sS ...'`; the token is never put on argv or echoed.

- Test output never prints a token, password or client secret. The default `scripts/check.sh` does not start Docker and stays green: the file is behind the e2e tag.

2. Write the test file with the subtests above on top of the DEX-04 helpers; run `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentitySmoke` and fix until green.

### 4/7 · W-P1-IDC-04

**Add the loopback CONNECT forwarder that injects a fresh identity token**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#303](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/303)

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26). A token placed in HTTPS_PROXY is readable by the agent's own tools and goes stale after about 1h. This ticket (#303) builds the piece that removes both limits: a CONNECT-only forwarder on loopback that holds the user's short-lived ID token in memory, asks the refreshing client (W-P1-IDC-02) for the current token on every new CONNECT, and injects it towards the worker. It was split from the original `identity exec` ticket (relabelled S to M by the audit): the forwarder library stays here and keeps issue #303; the command that starts the child process behind it, builds its environment and handles signals moved to W-P1-IDC-06. P2 extends exactly this forwarder with agent tokens (W-P2-RCP-02). It depends only on IDC-02. Out of scope: process supervision, the child environment, flags (IDC-06) and the L2 test (IDC-07).

What to build: internal/identityclient/forwarder.go and its tests. Nothing outside internal/identityclient changes.

**Requirements**

- New `internal/identityclient/forwarder.go`: `Forwarder{WorkerAddr string; Token func(ctx context.Context) (string, error); ClientCredential string; Now func() time.Time; Log *slog.Logger}` with `Serve(ctx context.Context, ln net.Listener) error` that returns when ctx is cancelled or the listener is closed. The token comes only from the Token callback (IDC-06 passes `Client.Token`: cache, refresh at 2/3 of exp-iat under the cache lock). It is held only in memory and never written to an environment, argv, file or log; logs carry only the 8-hex fingerprint.
- Only CONNECT is served (any other method gets 405). The CONNECT request is read with bounds that match the worker's own limits on main: request line at most 8 KiB (414), whole header block at most 64 KiB, 10 s deadline (431 on overflow, then close). Constants are named in forwarder.go and pinned by a test to those numbers.
- The client must present `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("wx:"+ClientCredential)`; the credential is checked with crypto/subtle constant-time compare and is never sent to the worker. A missing or wrong credential gets 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic` and no dial. Any other client header is dropped: the forwarder builds a fresh CONNECT for the worker containing only the request target, Host and `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)`.
- It dials ONLY `WorkerAddr` (10 s dial timeout) and never the CONNECT target. The worker's status line is relayed to the client verbatim (a 403 from the worker reaches the client as 403); on a 200 it splices bytes both ways with half-close handling and closes both sides when either ends.
- With no valid token (Token returns an error such as ErrLoginRequired or ErrIssuerUnreachable) the forwarder answers `503 Service Unavailable` with a short fixed body naming the failure class (never the error text) and makes no dial. A refresh failure for one CONNECT does not poison the next.
- Limitation recorded in the doc comment and in W-P1-IDC-01: attribution is bound per tunnel at CONNECT time, so a tunnel opened before a refresh keeps its original token; clients recycle connections. No refresh timer is needed: refreshing on demand per CONNECT through Client.Token (2/3 rule) gives the same guarantee without an extra goroutine (the alternative of a background timer was rejected).
- No new package, module or route (it lives in internal/identityclient from W-P1-IDC-02), so architecture.yaml needs no change.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/identityclient/forwarder_test.go with a fake CONNECT listener playing the worker, a fake clock and a rotating fake issuer behind a real identityclient.Client.
2. Implement internal/identityclient/forwarder.go: Forwarder, the bounded CONNECT reader, the credential check, the single worker dial, the verbatim status relay and the splice.
3. Add a doc comment describing the per-tunnel binding limitation and the pinned limits.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarder` shows the fake worker receives `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` even when the client sent its own, a GET gets 405, a 70 KiB CONNECT header block gets 431, a 9 KiB request line gets 414, a CONNECT without the per-run credential gets 407 and makes no dial, and dials go only to the worker address (never the CONNECT target).
- [ ] The worker's non-200 status line is relayed verbatim (403 stays 403) and a 200 splices data in both directions: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderRelay`.
- [ ] With a fake clock and a rotating fake issuer, a CONNECT made after 2/3 of the token lifetime carries the refreshed token while an earlier tunnel keeps working: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderRefresh`.
- [ ] With no valid token the client gets 503 and the fake worker records zero dials: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderNoToken`.
- [ ] Neither the token nor the per-run credential appears in captured logs or error strings: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderNoSecretsInLogs`.
- [ ] The limit constants equal the worker's: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderLimitsMatchWorker` (compares against the documented 8 KiB, 64 KiB and 10 s).
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-IDC-02`](identity-contract.md#27--w-p1-idc-02) Add internal/identityclient: config, discovery, device login, locked file cache, Token and Status

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-IDC-06`](identity-contract.md#67--w-p1-idc-06) Add `warden identity exec` to run a child behind the forwarder; [`W-P2-RCP-02`](identity-client.md#26--w-p2-rcp-02) Add the token-injecting forwarder and `warden identity forward`

### 5/7 · W-P1-IDC-05

**Add the `warden identity` cobra subtree: login, token, status, env and logout**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26). W-P1-IDC-02 (#28) ships the identityclient library; this ticket exposes it as the `warden identity` command tree and adds the proxy-env renderer. It was split from the original M ticket #28. It depends on IDC-02. Siblings: IDC-04 (forwarder) and IDC-06 (`identity exec`, which reuses the env renderer for CA variables), IDC-03 (L2 smoke that runs `identity env --token-stdin`), IDC-01 (docs). Adding the subtree changes nothing about `run` or `control-plane`; the worker and CP are untouched. cmd/ stays thin: logic lives in internal/identityclient.

What to build: cmd/proxy/identity.go with five subcommands registered in cmd/proxy/root.go, the env renderer in internal/identityclient/env.go, and the exit codes.

**Requirements**

- New cmd/proxy/identity.go: `newIdentityCmd()` with `login`, `token`, `status`, `env` and `logout`, registered in cmd/proxy/root.go next to the existing AddCommand calls. Persistent flags: `--issuer`, `--client-id` (default `warden-cli`), `--audience` (default `warden`), `--client-secret-env NAME` (there is NO flag taking a literal secret), `--scopes` (added to the defaults), `--cache-dir`, `--verbose` (there is no insecure-issuer flag: the http-issuer rule of W-P1-IDC-02 allows only loopback http issuers). The root `--config` is never loaded by this subtree.
- `token` prints the ID token to stdout only. `status` prints iss, sub, email, groups, exp and the cache path, never the token. `login` prints the verification URI and user code to stderr only. `logout` deletes the cache entry. Warnings from the library go to stderr.
- Exit codes: 2 means login is required (ErrLoginRequired); 3 means the issuer is unreachable and no valid cached token remains (ErrIssuerUnreachable); other errors exit 1.
- `env --worker host:port [--token-stdin | --token-file PATH] [--ca PATH] [--shell sh|fish|powershell] [--format dotenv|json] [--include-http]` prints HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy built with url.UserPassword("session", token), plus NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1. `--ca` adds SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. HTTP_PROXY is printed only with `--include-http`, with a note that the worker denies plain http. The token comes from the cache, `--token-stdin` or `--token-file`; it is NEVER accepted as an argv value. The token expiry and a warning that child processes can read the token go to stderr. The renderer is new `internal/identityclient/env.go` (`ProxyEnv(worker, token, opts)` for sh, fish, powershell, dotenv and json) so IDC-06 reuses it. Transparent-mode workers need no proxy variables; the help text says `env` is for explicit-proxy agents.
- Only `token` and `env` write secrets, and only to stdout. By default nothing is logged except errors. `--verbose` logs issuer, client_id, scopes, expiry and the 8-hex sha256 fingerprint, never a raw token, device code or IdP error body.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing cmd tests first (cmd/proxy/identity_test.go with a captured slog handler and stderr buffer) and the renderer tests in internal/identityclient/env_test.go.
2. Add internal/identityclient/env.go (ProxyEnv and the shell/format renderers).
3. Add cmd/proxy/identity.go and register it in cmd/proxy/root.go; map ErrLoginRequired and ErrIssuerUnreachable to exit codes 2 and 3.
4. Run the whole cmd/proxy suite to confirm `run` and `control-plane` are unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestEnvConnectHeader` builds an http.Transport with http.ProxyURL from parsed `env` output and an httptest CONNECT listener sees `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)`; the default output contains no HTTP_PROXY, and `--include-http` adds it.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestProxyEnvFormats` covers sh, fish, powershell, dotenv and json output, quoting of special characters in the token and CA path, and `--ca` variables.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityCmd` confirms the five subcommands are registered, no flag takes a literal client secret, the root `--config` is not read, `--token` is rejected as an argv value, and with `--verbose` captured stderr and logs contain no substring of the ID, refresh or device code values.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExitCodes` shows exit 2 when login is required and exit 3 when the issuer is down with no valid cache, using a fake issuer.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy` passes unchanged for the existing subcommands, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 6/7 · W-P1-IDC-06

**Add `warden identity exec` to run a child behind the forwarder**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26). The forwarder (W-P1-IDC-04, issue #303) injects a fresh identity token into every CONNECT; this ticket is the command that makes it usable: `warden identity exec --worker host:port -- <cmd>` starts the forwarder on loopback, runs the child with HTTPS_PROXY pointing at it, and supervises the child. The user's token is therefore never in the parent's or the child's environment or argv. It was split from the original `identity exec` ticket #303. It depends on IDC-04 (forwarder) and IDC-05 (the `identity` subtree and the env renderer for CA variables). Siblings: IDC-07 (L2 test), IDC-01 (docs). P2 later adds `--agent-id` and `--run-as` to this command (W-P2-RCP-06). Out of scope: the forwarder internals and the cache/refresh logic.

What to build: cmd/proxy/identity_exec.go (flags and wiring only) and internal/identityclient/exec.go (child environment builder and process supervisor).

**Requirements**

- `warden identity exec --worker host:port [--listen 127.0.0.1:0] [--ca PATH] [--include-http] -- <cmd> [args]` in the IDC-05 `identity` subtree. A non-loopback `--listen` is refused before any child starts. The token is never accepted as a flag, environment variable or argv value.
- The per-run proxy credential is 128 random bits from crypto/rand, generated per run, handed to the Forwarder as ClientCredential and to the child only inside `http://wx:<credential>@127.0.0.1:<port>`. The ID token itself never reaches the exec process's environment, the child's environment or argv, files or logs (fingerprint only with `--verbose`).
- Child environment builder (new internal/identityclient/exec.go): HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy set to the loopback URL; NO_PROXY and no_proxy = localhost,127.0.0.1,::1; HTTP_PROXY only with `--include-http`; inherited ALL_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY (any case) and WARDEN_IDENTITY_* are removed, with a stderr warning when an existing HTTPS_PROXY is overridden; `--ca` adds the same CA variables as `warden identity env` through the IDC-05 renderer.
- Process handling: stdio is inherited; SIGTERM and SIGHUP are forwarded to the child; SIGINT and SIGQUIT are forwarded only when stdin is not a terminal (a terminal delivers them to the foreground group itself). The exit code is the child's, or 128+signo when a signal killed it. When the cache needs a login at start (ErrLoginRequired): a terminal runs the device-code login on stderr; otherwise exec exits 2 without starting the child. The forwarder stops and the listener closes when the child exits.
- Documented limitation (docs via IDC-01): a same-uid child can still read the identity cache file; use a separate uid or the P2 `--run-as`. No new package, module or route.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/identityclient/exec.go: BuildChildEnv(parent []string, proxyURL, opts) and Run(ctx, spec) (exitCode int, err error) with signal handling behind an interface so it is unit-testable.
2. New cmd/proxy/identity_exec.go: flag parsing, loopback listener, credential generation, wiring Client.Token into Forwarder.Token, login-on-terminal behaviour; register in the identity subtree.
3. Tests: internal/identityclient/exec_test.go (env builder, signals with a fake process), cmd/proxy/identity_exec_test.go with the helper-process pattern (the child prints its env and argv).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExec` shows the child's env and argv contain the loopback HTTPS_PROXY with the per-run credential and no substring of the ID or refresh token, `--listen 0.0.0.0:0` is refused before any child starts, `exec -- sh -c 'exit 7'` exits 7, a child killed by SIGTERM exits 143, and a non-terminal run with no cached login exits 2 without starting the child.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestBuildChildEnv` shows inherited proxy variables and WARDEN_IDENTITY_* are removed, the override warning is emitted, NO_PROXY is set, HTTP_PROXY appears only with `--include-http` and CA variables appear with `--ca`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExecSignals` shows SIGTERM and SIGHUP are forwarded, and SIGINT only when stdin is not a terminal.
- [ ] End to end in-process: a child `curl`-like helper dialing through the loopback URL reaches a fake worker that sees `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)`: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecThroughForwarder`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate.

### 7/7 · W-P1-IDC-07

**Add the L2 test for `warden identity exec` attribution**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue —

Context: feature p1-identity-contract (epic #26). The feature's done-when says `warden identity exec --worker <worker> -- curl https://<allowed host>` is attributed to the same user while the child's environment and argv contain no token. W-P1-IDC-03 proves the `env` path; this ticket proves the `exec` path on the same real stack. It is new (created by the P1 split pass); no earlier ticket covered the exec done-when with a test beyond unit level. Depends on IDC-03 (the identity config and the smoke it extends) and IDC-06 (the command). Refresh behaviour while a child runs is proven by the unit test TestForwarderRefresh (Dex tokens last 1h, too long for an L2 test). Out of scope: any code change.

What to build: tests in `test/e2e/identity/identity_exec_test.go` (build tag e2e) named `TestIdentityExec*`.

**Requirements**

- Seed the identity cache inside agent-1: a helper in test/e2e/identity builds an `identityclient.Entry` (IDC-02) from a Dex token for alice obtained on the host with the Go `dexToken` helper (plain `http://localhost:5556`, no dialer override) using client `agent-harness` (scope with offline_access, so a refresh token exists) and writes it, through the library's FileStore format, into a 0700 directory as a 0600 file via `docker compose exec -T agent-1 sh -c 'cat > ...; chmod 600 ...'`. agent-1 has no route to Dex, so the container is given no issuer URL for Dex and never refreshes: the seeded cache is its only token source. The command then runs with `--client-id agent-harness --client-secret-env HARNESS_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET` and `--cache-dir` pointing at that directory.
- `TestIdentityExecAttributed`: run `warden identity exec --worker worker-1:8080 --ca /etc/warden/certs/proxy-ca.crt -- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<allowed host>/` in agent-1; expect 200 and a CP event (polled via `cpTraffic` with `?user=<alice's email>`) with identity_status valid and alice's sub.
- `TestIdentityExecChildSecrets`: run `exec -- sh -c 'env; tr "\0" " " < /proc/$$/cmdline'` in agent-1; the output contains the loopback `HTTPS_PROXY` and contains neither the ID token nor the refresh token nor any JWT-shaped string; the parent process's `/proc/<pid>/environ` and cmdline (read by a second `docker compose exec` while the child sleeps) hold neither.
- `TestIdentityExecNoLogin`: with an empty cache directory and no TTY, exec exits 2 and the child never starts (a marker file is absent).
- Output never prints tokens or secrets; the leak sweep over worker logs from IDC-03 is reused.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the cache-seeding helper and the three tests (each starting with `requireStack(t)`) in test/e2e/identity/identity_exec_test.go.
2. Run `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentityExec` until green; mutate by adding the token to the child env in a scratch build and confirm TestIdentityExecChildSecrets fails.

- [ ] `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentityExec` passes on a machine with Docker.
- [ ] Red first: a scratch build of `identity exec` that exports the ID token in the child's environment makes `TestIdentityExecChildSecrets` fail.
